title: Greenwashing Auditor data contract
description: Root schema validates one Event (one line of an event log). The envelope (seq, t_ms, type, payload) is owned by the transport and documented in fixtures/README.md; this schema restates it and defines every payload. The Analysis object, the entities and the enums live in definitions. Contract version 1.0.0; see CONTRACT.md.

Id.description: Stable identifier. Fixture ids are short (C1, L11, E8b, X3, O2); live ids may be generated. Unique across all entity types within one analysis.

Ext.description: Free extension bag. Anything not in the contract goes here so additionalProperties can stay false everywhere else.

Span.description: A verbatim substring of Document.text. `text` is authoritative; `start`/`end` are Unicode code-point offsets into Document.text and must satisfy text == Document.text[start:end]. `context` and `occurrence` are authoring hints used to re-anchor the span if offsets go stale.

context.description: A unique substring of Document.text that contains `text`; disambiguates repeated phrases.

occurrence.description: 1-based index of which occurrence of `text` in Document.text is meant, when `context` is not given.

Region.description: A labelled range of Document.text. Regions of the same kind must not overlap; different kinds may nest (a paragraph may contain list_items). Used for prominence weighting and for scrolling to paragraph labels.

label.description: Human label such as P4 or 'Cautionary note'.

prominence.description: 1.0 = headline/hero, 0.6 = body, 0.3 = footnote or cautionary note.

sasb_codes.description: SASB industry codes used as the materiality reference, e.g. EM-EP.

TextType.description: The brief's kinds (label, policy, claim) plus common concrete forms.

method.description: How the text was obtained (e.g. AEM model JSON, static HTML, PDF).

fixture_path.description: Repo path of the saved text, if any.

text.description: Canonical plain text. Rules: NFC-normalised; every Unicode space character (including U+00A0) becomes an ASCII space; no tabs or carriage returns; no runs of spaces; \n line breaks; blocks separated by exactly one blank line; no leading or trailing whitespace; no markdown markers. All spans index into this string by Unicode code point.

ClaimType.description: D4 Q1. Routes evaluation: factual claims are verified; commitments tested for credibility; comparatives need their baseline; certifications checked for existence and coverage; vague attributes are unverifiable by construction.

spans.description: First span is the primary highlight; further spans are repeats of the same claim elsewhere in the text.

scope_note.description: Precise scope in words, e.g. 'operated upstream assets only'.

attribute.description: What is asserted: net zero, -36%, cleaner, ...

paragraph.description: Label of the paragraph region the primary span sits in (P1...).

SignalKind.description: D4 Q2. Claim-level kinds are the first fourteen; prominence, share_of_attention, emotive and register may also be document-level.

Polarity.description: flag = a greenwashing signal; benign = noted but harmless (so the Language layer visibly does not flag everything); credit = a qualifier or precision that counts in the text's favour.

spans.description: Word-level marks. Required non-empty for level=claim; may be empty for level=document.

Tier.description: D5 reliability tier. 1 regulator ruling, court judgment, law; 2 audited/assured filing, government or intergovernmental data; 3 independent third-party dataset or standard; 4 news; 5 the company's own material.

Relation.description: From the target's point of view. supports/contradicts concern the literal content; contradicts_framing means the literal content stands but the impression does not; context is background or materiality; precedent is a ruling on similar wording; criteria is a rule the claim is measured against. For an omission target, supports means the evidence establishes the omitted fact.

Verification.description: fetched_exact: quote matched programmatically against the fetched source; fetched_by_eye: read from the fetched source by a person; second_party_fetch: fetched and quoted by a separate verification run; computed: the item is a computation, its quote is the result statement and its verification rests on derived_from; unverified: never displayed as a quote.

date.description: Publication or decision date, ISO date or free text if only a year/month is known.

locator.description: Page, paragraph, section or case reference.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the source. Displayed only when verified.

stage.description: Which evaluator produced or found it.

target.description: A claim id or an omission id.

computation.description: For kind=computation: a number recomputed from other evidence.

derived_from.description: Evidence ids this item was computed from.

Dimension.description: D6 claim-level dimensions. Completeness is document-level and lives in Summary.

DimensionScore.description: score is a problem score: 0 = no greenwashing signal on this dimension, 1 = maximal. confidence is how sure the evaluator is of that score.

Tag.description: The seven sins of greenwashing plus greenrinsing (a target changed before it is met, from Planet Tracker's taxonomy).

Verdict.description: likelihood = max of the claim's four dimension scores (weakest link). category is derived from the scores and the evidence relations by the rule in CONTRACT.md §6.

rationale.description: The judge's reasoning, one to three sentences.

fix.description: What evidence or rewording would make the claim legitimate.

rewrite.description: The claim as the evidence would allow it to be stated.

topic.description: Short title for the margin card: 'Not mentioned: ...'.

materiality_reference.description: The external reference that makes it material, e.g. 'SASB EM-EP: Reserves Valuation & Capital Expenditures'.

complete_text.description: What the document would say if it were complete.

headline.description: score is the document's greenwashing likelihood.

target.description: Claim or omission id; the header links to it.

DimensionProfile.description: The five D6 dimensions, each with its own score and confidence. Completeness is document-level, so at claim level it has no score of its own.

VerdictDistribution.description: How many claims fell into each verdict category. Must equal the verdicts counted.

TrendDirection.description: Which way the headline moved between the company's oldest and newest document. Scores are problem scores, so `worsening` means the headline went up. `undetermined` is for fewer than two dated documents: a company with one page has not held still, it has not been watched.

TrendPoint.description: One end of the trend: the document whose headline it is, when that document is from, and what it read.

CompanyTrend.description: The movement of the headline across one company's documents in time order, with a separate confidence saying how much of it to believe and a note that says so in words. Two documents are a line, not a trend: `confidence` is low and `note` says why, and a page must show one with the other.

points.description: Documents the direction rests on: those that carry a date.

change.description: last.score - first.score. Null when there are fewer than two points.

per_year.description: The change at an annual rate. Null when there are fewer than two points or they share a date.

span_days.description: Days between the first and last point.

confidence.description: How much of the direction to believe: 0 when undetermined, and never above the confidence of the two headlines that moved.

first.description: The oldest point. Both ends are the same document when only one carries a date, and both are null when none does.

note.description: One sentence a page can print under the arrow, saying what the direction rests on — including, when it rests on two documents, that two documents are not a trend.

CompanyDocument.description: One analysed document as the company view lists it: its own header numbers, what it is worth in the company's (recency x confidence) and how much of the company's headline it is (share). Documents are listed oldest first.

document_id.description: Document.id of the analysed document; half of a company-level target, since claim ids repeat across analyses.

date.description: When the document is from. Absent when neither an archive capture nor a retrieval date says; `date_basis` then reads `unknown` and the document is left off the trend.

date_basis.description: Where `date` came from. `archive` wins over `retrieved`, because the ingester stamps `retrieved` with the day it ran even when it read a 2024 capture.

recency.description: How current this document is against the company's newest: 1.0 for that one, halving every half-life before it. The company-level analogue of a claim's prominence.

weight.description: recency x the headline's confidence: this document's say in every company number.

share.description: This document's share of the company headline. The shares add up to 1.

CompanyView.description: One company's analyses side by side, with the trend over time (D2's third zoom level, D6 "Aggregation"). Served by GET /api/company/{name} and built by backend/auditor/company.py; not part of an event stream, because it spans analyses. Every number is arithmetic over the documents listed beneath it and records its contributors in ext.drivers; only the narrative is written.

headline.description: score is the company's greenwashing likelihood across the documents analysed. It says what the worst of the record is; the trend says which way it is moving.

documents.description: Every document of this company that has a complete analysis, oldest first: the trend's order.

top_issues.description: The company's worst findings across its documents, ranked by the same weighted severity the aggregation uses. A target is (document_id, target): claim and omission ids are unique within one analysis only.

target.description: Claim or omission id inside that document's analysis.

title.description: The title that document's own summary gave the finding.

credit.description: Credit where due across the documents: well-substantiated claims.

narrative.description: The one thing asked of a model, after the numbers are fixed. Absent when nobody has written one: GET /api/company/{name} serves arithmetic only, so no page waits on a model.

Stage.description: Pipeline stages, in canonical order, named as in fixtures/README.md. language = Linguistic evaluator (D5), substantiate = Substantiation evaluator, verify = External verification, consistency = Self-consistency. The four evaluators and omissions may run concurrently after extract; verdict waits for all of them; summary waits for verdict.

Analysis.description: The folded result of one analysis: what the frontend holds in memory after consuming the event log, and what the fixture is authored as.

analysis_id.description: From analysis.started.payload.analysis_id in a fixture; the server's id for a live run.

Event.description: One line of the event log: the transport envelope (fixtures/README.md) with a contract payload. seq may be omitted in files (assigned from line order); t_ms is milliseconds since analysis.started, non-decreasing.

P_AnalysisStarted.description: Descriptive keys are allowed (the transport adds `source`). contract_version is required so a consumer can refuse a log it does not understand.

label.description: Human text for the progress display, e.g. 'Finding claims'.

final.description: True for the last summary of the analysis; earlier ones are provisional and may be replaced.

P_DebugNote.description: Free-form note for the debug drawer.
